items.title: Show HN: HackerBooks – HackerTube, but for books mentioned on HN
items.author: roansh
items.excerpt: Saw Karpathy's HackerTube and wanted the same thing for books. So I had Claude build one (Opus 5.5).It's ~16.5k books that at least two different HN commenters brought up, from 2007 till now. Each book links back to the comments that mentioned it. Data is downloadable from the about page.To be clear: Claude wrote almost all of it, including the data pipeline and the site. I mostly steered and made calls, bought the domain name, etc.It counts mentions, so it's not perfect (praising a book and trashing it both count). If your favourite book is missing or matched to the wrong thing, tell me. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50326821 Points: 733 # Comments: 160
items.why_it_matters: A Show HN side project mostly built by Claude Opus 5.5. It is a mild example of agent-driven building, but it offers no technical depth or workflow lessons.

items.title: Quoting Kyle Kingsbury
items.excerpt: More broadly, the use of LLMs erodes trust in documentation, in software, and in the organizations which produce them. Perhaps engineers will begin to treat any new software project with suspicion—the signals we used to rely on as markers of a mature system are now easier to counterfeit. [...] In the age of LLMs, what can maintainers do to ensure correct software and accurate documentation? Having done that work, how can they demonstrate its quality to users? — Kyle Kingsbury, Jepsen results for ParticleDB 1.1.4 Tags: kyle-kingsbury, llms, ai, generative-ai, ai-misuse
items.why_it_matters: Kingsbury on LLMs eroding trust in software and docs fits our verification-over-vibes stance and is useful framing for CTOs advising clients on AI-generated code quality.
